meta.topic: 光滑流形、切空间与切映射、向量场与流、微分形式、外微分、流形积分

zh: 设 $M$ 是拓扑空间。若对每点 $p\in M$ 都存在开邻域 $U$ 与同胚 $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$（$\varphi(U)$ 为开集），则称 $(U,\varphi)$ 为一张坐标卡；覆盖 $M$ 的一族坐标卡称为图册。约定 $M$ 为 Hausdorff 且第二可数。局部模型 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 的 $n$ 由 Brouwer 区域不变性唯一确定，故维数是流形的内蕴不变量。此时 $M$ 只是拓扑流形：同胚只保证连续，尚不能求导。

设 $(U_\alpha,\varphi_\alpha)$、$(U_\beta,\varphi_\beta)$ 是两张图且 $U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\ne\varnothing$。转换函数 $$\begin{aligned}\varphi_{\beta\alpha}&:=\varphi_\beta\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1}:\\ \varphi_\alpha(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)&\longrightarrow\varphi_\beta(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta).\end{aligned}$$ 是 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 两个开集之间的同胚。若图册中每一对转换函数都是 $C^\infty$，称之为光滑图册。三张图相交时，在重叠区有恒等式 $\varphi_{\gamma\beta}\circ\varphi_{\beta\alpha}=\varphi_{\gamma\alpha}$；由于 $C^\infty$ 映射的复合仍为 $C^\infty$，逐对验证光滑性是相容的，不会因增补图表而破坏。

定义 $f:M\to\mathbb{R}$ 光滑，是指对图册中每张图 $(U,\varphi)$，$f\circ\varphi^{-1}$ 在 $\varphi(U)$ 上 $C^\infty$。验证与图无关：若 $f\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1}$ 光滑，则在重叠区 $$f\circ\varphi_\beta^{-1}=(f\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1})\circ(\varphi_\alpha\circ\varphi_\beta^{-1}),$$ 右端是两个 $C^\infty$ 映射在开集上的复合，故光滑。条件「转换函数光滑」正是这一步的全部依据；若只有连续转换，$f\circ\varphi_\beta^{-1}$ 未必可微，「光滑函数」就不良定义。

同一图册还能把各点的切空间粘成整体。令 $TM=\bigsqcup_{p\in M}T_pM$，图 $(U_\alpha,\varphi_\alpha)$ 给出局部平凡化（$\pi:TM\to M$ 为投影） $$\begin{aligned}\Phi_\alpha:\pi^{-1}(U_\alpha)&\to\varphi_\alpha(U_\alpha)\times\mathbb{R}^n,\\ \sum_i v^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x_\alpha^i}\Big|_p&\mapsto\bigl(\varphi_\alpha(p),v^1,\dots,v^n\bigr).\end{aligned}$$ 在重叠区，$\Phi_\beta\circ\Phi_\alpha^{-1}(x,v)=\bigl(\varphi_{\beta\alpha}(x),\,D\varphi_{\beta\alpha}(x)v\bigr)$。由于 $\varphi_{\beta\alpha}$ 光滑，其雅可比 $D\varphi_{\beta\alpha}$ 光滑，且对 $v$ 线性；故 $TM$ 是 $2n$ 维光滑流形，投影 $\pi$ 光滑。结论：光滑结构足以沿转换函数搬运一切线性代数构造（$TM$、$T^*M$、$\Lambda^kT^*M$）。

例：$S^n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}:|x|=1\}$。令 $N=(0,\dots,0,1)$、$S=-N$，定义球极投影 $$ egin{aligned}\sigma_N(x)&= rac{(x_1,\dots,x_n)}{1-x_{n+1}}\quad(x
e N),\ \sigma_S(x)&= rac{(x_1,\dots,x_n)}{1+x_{n+1}}\quad(x
e S).\end{aligned}$$ 二者分别同胚于 $\mathbb{R}^n$，且 $S^n=(S^n\setminus\{N\})\cup(S^n\setminus\{S\})$。在重叠区 $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$ 上直接代入得 $\sigma_S\circ\sigma_N^{-1}(u)=u/|u|^2$，其分量是有理函数、分母 $|u|^2
e0$，故 $C^\infty$。因此这两张图构成光滑图册，$S^n$ 是 $n$ 维光滑流形。

带边情形把局部模型换成上半空间 $\mathbb{H}^n=\{x_n\ge0\}$，坐标卡取值于 $\mathbb{H}^n$ 的开集。称 $p$ 为边界点（$p\in\partial M$），若某张（从而每张）图中 $\varphi(p)$ 满足 $x_n=0$：这一判定与图无关，因为边界点没有同胚于 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 的邻域，而内点有（区域不变性）。以 $\varphi|_{\partial M}$ 为图，$\partial M$ 是 $(n-1)$ 维无边流形，$\partial(\partial M)=\varnothing$。注意光滑结构是额外结构而非拓扑必然：Milnor 怪球与 $S^7$ 同胚但光滑结构不同，四维拓扑流形甚至可能没有光滑结构；Hausdorff 与第二可数则保证仿紧性与单位分解，后者是整体构造（度规、积分）的工具。
en: Let $M$ be a topological space. If every $p\in M$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ and a homeomorphism $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ onto an open set, then $(U,\varphi)$ is a chart, and a family of charts covering $M$ is an atlas. We assume $M$ is Hausdorff and second-countable. The $n$ of the local model is unique by Brouwer's invariance of domain, so the dimension is an intrinsic invariant. At this stage $M$ is only a topological manifold: homeomorphisms preserve continuity but do not permit differentiation.

Let $(U_\alpha,\varphi_\alpha)$ and $(U_\beta,\varphi_\beta)$ be charts with $U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\ne\varnothing$. The transition map $$\begin{aligned}\varphi_{\beta\alpha}&:=\varphi_\beta\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1}:\\ \varphi_\alpha(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)&\longrightarrow\varphi_\beta(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta).\end{aligned}$$ is a homeomorphism between open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. An atlas is smooth if every transition map is $C^\infty$. On triple overlaps the cocycle identity $\varphi_{\gamma\beta}\circ\varphi_{\beta\alpha}=\varphi_{\gamma\alpha}$ holds; since compositions of $C^\infty$ maps are $C^\infty$, checking smoothness pairwise is consistent and remains valid when charts are added.

A map $f:M\to\mathbb{R}$ is smooth if for every chart $(U,\varphi)$ in the atlas the composition $f\circ\varphi^{-1}$ is $C^\infty$ on $\varphi(U)$. This is chart-independent: if $f\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1}$ is smooth, then on the overlap $$f\circ\varphi_\beta^{-1}=(f\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1})\circ(\varphi_\alpha\circ\varphi_\beta^{-1}),$$ and the right side is a composition of $C^\infty$ maps on open sets, hence smooth. Smoothness of transition maps is exactly what this step uses; with merely continuous transitions $f\circ\varphi_\beta^{-1}$ need not be differentiable and “smooth function” would be ill-defined.

The same atlas glues the tangent spaces into a global object. Let $TM=\bigsqcup_{p\in M}T_pM$. A chart $(U_\alpha,\varphi_\alpha)$ gives a local trivialization ($\pi:TM\to M$ the projection) $$\begin{aligned}\Phi_\alpha:\pi^{-1}(U_\alpha)&\to\varphi_\alpha(U_\alpha)\times\mathbb{R}^n,\\ \sum_i v^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x_\alpha^i}\Big|_p&\mapsto\bigl(\varphi_\alpha(p),v^1,\dots,v^n\bigr).\end{aligned}$$ On overlaps, $\Phi_\beta\circ\Phi_\alpha^{-1}(x,v)=\bigl(\varphi_{\beta\alpha}(x),\,D\varphi_{\beta\alpha}(x)v\bigr)$. Since $\varphi_{\beta\alpha}$ is smooth, its Jacobian $D\varphi_{\beta\alpha}$ is smooth and linear in $v$; hence $TM$ is a smooth $2n$-manifold and $\pi$ is smooth. Thus the smooth structure suffices to transport every linear-algebraic construction ($TM$, $T^*M$, $\Lambda^kT^*M$).

Example: $S^n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}:|x|=1\}$. Put $N=(0,\dots,0,1)$ and $S=-N$, and define the stereographic projections $$ egin{aligned}\sigma_N(x)&= rac{(x_1,\dots,x_n)}{1-x_{n+1}}\quad(x
e N),\ \sigma_S(x)&= rac{(x_1,\dots,x_n)}{1+x_{n+1}}\quad(x
e S).\end{aligned}$$ Each is a homeomorphism onto $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $S^n=(S^n\setminus\{N\})\cup(S^n\setminus\{S\})$. On the overlap $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$ direct substitution gives $\sigma_S\circ\sigma_N^{-1}(u)=u/|u|^2$, whose components are rational functions with denominator $|u|^2
e0$, hence $C^\infty$. Thus these two charts form a smooth atlas and $S^n$ is a smooth $n$-manifold.

For manifolds with boundary the local model becomes the half-space $\mathbb{H}^n=\{x_n\ge0\}$, with charts taking values in open subsets of $\mathbb{H}^n$. A point $p$ lies in $\partial M$ if in some (hence every) chart $\varphi(p)$ has $x_n=0$: this is chart-independent because a boundary point has no neighbourhood homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^n$, whereas an interior point does (invariance of domain). With the restrictions $\varphi|_{\partial M}$ as charts, $\partial M$ is an $(n-1)$-manifold without boundary and $\partial(\partial M)=\varnothing$. Note that a smooth structure is extra structure, not a topological necessity: Milnor's exotic spheres are homeomorphic to $S^7$ but smoothly distinct, and some four-dimensional topological manifolds admit no smooth structure at all; Hausdorff and second-countability guarantee paracompactness and partitions of unity, the tools for global constructions (metrics, integration).

zh: 固定 $p\in M$。考虑光滑曲线 $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\to M$，$\gamma(0)=p$。取含 $p$ 的图 $(U,\varphi)$，规定 $\gamma_1\sim\gamma_2\iff(\varphi\circ\gamma_1)'(0)=(\varphi\circ\gamma_2)'(0)$。换图 $\psi$ 时，链式法则给出 $$\begin{aligned}(\psi\circ\gamma)'(0)&=D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)\\&\quad\cdot\bigl[(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(0)\bigr].\end{aligned}$$ 右端是固定线性映射作用在速度上，故在一个图中相等蕴含在另一个图中相等；又 $\sim$ 显然是等价关系。于是等价类 $[\gamma]$ 与图无关，定义为 $p$ 处的切向量，全体记 $T_pM$。

用图把 $T_pM$ 与 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 对齐：$\Theta_\varphi([\gamma])=(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(0)$。由第 1 步它是双射。定义 $$\begin{aligned}\,[\gamma_1]+[\gamma_2]&:=\Theta_\varphi^{-1}\bigl(\Theta_\varphi[\gamma_1]+\Theta_\varphi[\gamma_2]\bigr),\\ c\,[\gamma]&:=\Theta_\varphi^{-1}\bigl(c\,\Theta_\varphi[\gamma]\bigr).\end{aligned}$$ 需检验与图无关：换图后 $\Theta_\psi\circ\Theta_\varphi^{-1}=D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})(\varphi(p))$ 是线性同构，线性运算在可逆线性映射下保持，故所得向量空间结构与图无关。结论：$T_pM$ 是 $n$ 维实向量空间，零向量是常值曲线的类；几何上 $[\gamma]$ 就是曲线在 $p$ 的速度。

另一条路线：称线性映射 $v:C^\infty(M)\to\mathbb{R}$ 为 $p$ 处的导子，若满足莱布尼茨法则 $v(fg)=f(p)v(g)+g(p)v(f)$。由 $[\gamma]\mapsto\bigl(f\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(0)\bigr)$ 得到导子：线性显然，乘积法则给出莱布尼茨。反之设 $v$ 是导子。先用截断函数可证 $v(f)$ 只依赖 $f$ 在 $p$ 附近的值，故可在局部讨论。取图并以 $x^i$ 记坐标函数（必要时用截断函数把 $x^i$ 延拓到整个 $M$，这不改变 $p$ 附近的取值），对 $f$ 用带积分余项的泰勒公式，在 $p$ 的邻域内 $$\begin{aligned}f&=f(p)+\sum_{i=1}^n x^i g_i,\\ g_i(p)&=\frac{\partial(f\circ\varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\Big|_{\varphi(p)}.\end{aligned}$$ 由 $v(\text{常数})=0$ 与 $x^i(p)=0$，莱布尼茨法则给出 $$v(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n v(x^i)g_i(p)+\sum_{i=1}^n x^i(p)v(g_i)=\sum_{i=1}^n v(x^i)g_i(p),$$ 故 $v$ 由数组 $(v(x^1),\dots,v(x^n))$ 完全决定。取曲线使 $\Theta_\varphi([\gamma])=(v(x^1),\dots,v(x^n))$，即得 $v=v_\gamma$。结论：$T_pM\cong\mathrm{Der}_p(C^\infty(M))$ 为线性同构。

取图 $(U,\varphi)$，坐标函数 $x^i=u^i\circ\varphi$。定义 $$\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p(f):=\frac{\partial(f\circ\varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr).$$ 由第 3 步的公式，每个 $v\in T_pM$ 可唯一写成 $$v=\sum_{i=1}^n v^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,\qquad v^i=v(x^i)=dx^i(v),$$ 故这 $n$ 个向量构成基，$\dim T_pM=n$。换图 $y=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}(x)$ 时链式法则给出 $$\frac{\partial}{\partial y^j}\Big|_p=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^j}\bigl(\psi(p)\bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,$$ 即切向量的坐标按 $v^i=\sum_j\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^j}w^j$ 变换（反变），变换矩阵可逆。

设 $F:M\to N$ 光滑。定义 $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ 为 $dF_p[\gamma]:=[F\circ\gamma]$。良定义：若 $\gamma_1\sim\gamma_2$，取 $p$、$F(p)$ 附近的图，$F$ 的坐标表示 $\tilde F=\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}$ 光滑，则 $$(\psi\circ F\circ\gamma_i)'(0)=D\tilde F\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)\bigl[(\varphi\circ\gamma_i)'(0)\bigr],$$ 两个速度相等故像速度相等。$dF_p$ 线性（坐标中就是乘固定矩阵），且 $$d(G\circ F)_p=dG_{F(p)}\circ dF_p,\qquad d(\mathrm{id}_M)_p=\mathrm{id}.$$ 用导子写就是 $(dF_p v)(g)=v(g\circ F)$，$g\in C^\infty(N)$。结论：切映射把 $M$ 的切方向推到 $N$，复合对应矩阵相乘。

在基下写出矩阵：设 $y^j=F^j(x)$，则 $$dF_p\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p\Bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\partial F^j}{\partial x^i}(p)\frac{\partial}{\partial y^j}\Big|_{F(p)},$$ 即 $dF_p$ 的矩阵是雅可比矩阵 $(\partial F^j/\partial x^i)$，故 $\operatorname{rank}dF_p$ 与图无关。若 $\dim M=\dim N=n$ 且 $dF_p$ 可逆，则由反函数定理 $F$ 在 $p$ 附近是微分同胚，且 $(dF_p)^{-1}=d(F^{-1})_{F(p)}$。例：$S^2=F^{-1}(1)$，$F(x)=|x|^2$，$dF_p=2p^{\mathsf T}\ne0$，由正则水平集定理，$T_pS^2=\ker dF_p=\{v:v\cdot p=0\}=p^\perp$。注意方向：切映射只把 $T_pM$ 送到 $T_{F(p)}N$；当 $F$ 不是单射时，向量场一般不能整体推前，而形式总可以拉回。
en: Fix $p\in M$ and consider smooth curves $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=p$. Relative to a chart $(U,\varphi)$ around $p$, declare $\gamma_1\sim\gamma_2\iff(\varphi\circ\gamma_1)'(0)=(\varphi\circ\gamma_2)'(0)$. For another chart $\psi$, the chain rule gives $$\begin{aligned}(\psi\circ\gamma)'(0)&=D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)\\&\quad\cdot\bigl[(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(0)\bigr].\end{aligned}$$ where a fixed linear map acts on the velocity, so equality in one chart implies equality in the other; and $\sim$ is plainly an equivalence relation. Hence the class $[\gamma]$ is chart-independent; it is called a tangent vector at $p$, and the set of all classes is $T_pM$.

Use a chart to identify $T_pM$ with $\mathbb{R}^n$: $\Theta_\varphi([\gamma])=(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(0)$, a bijection by Step 1. Set $$\begin{aligned}\,[\gamma_1]+[\gamma_2]&:=\Theta_\varphi^{-1}\bigl(\Theta_\varphi[\gamma_1]+\Theta_\varphi[\gamma_2]\bigr),\\ c\,[\gamma]&:=\Theta_\varphi^{-1}\bigl(c\,\Theta_\varphi[\gamma]\bigr).\end{aligned}$$ This is chart-independent: after a change of chart $\Theta_\psi\circ\Theta_\varphi^{-1}=D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})(\varphi(p))$ is a linear isomorphism, and linear operations are preserved under invertible linear maps, so the vector-space structure does not depend on the chart. Hence $T_pM$ is an $n$-dimensional real vector space, its zero vector being the class of a constant curve; geometrically $[\gamma]$ is the velocity of the curve at $p$.

Alternative route: a linear map $v:C^\infty(M)\to\mathbb{R}$ is a derivation at $p$ if it satisfies the Leibniz rule $v(fg)=f(p)v(g)+g(p)v(f)$. The map $[\gamma]\mapsto\bigl(f\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(0)\bigr)$ produces derivations: linearity is clear and the product rule gives Leibniz. Conversely, let $v$ be a derivation. A cutoff-function argument shows that $v(f)$ depends only on $f$ near $p$, so the discussion may be local. Take a chart with coordinate functions $x^i$ (extend them over $M$ by cutoff functions if necessary; this does not change their values near $p$) and apply Taylor's formula with integral remainder near $p$: $$\begin{aligned}f&=f(p)+\sum_{i=1}^n x^i g_i,\\ g_i(p)&=\frac{\partial(f\circ\varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\Big|_{\varphi(p)}.\end{aligned}$$ Since $v(\text{constant})=0$ and $x^i(p)=0$, the Leibniz rule gives $$v(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n v(x^i)g_i(p)+\sum_{i=1}^n x^i(p)v(g_i)=\sum_{i=1}^n v(x^i)g_i(p),$$ so $v$ is determined by the array $(v(x^1),\dots,v(x^n))$. Choosing a curve with $\Theta_\varphi([\gamma])=(v(x^1),\dots,v(x^n))$ gives $v=v_\gamma$. Hence $T_pM\cong\mathrm{Der}_p(C^\infty(M))$ linearly.

Take a chart $(U,\varphi)$ with coordinate functions $x^i=u^i\circ\varphi$ and define $$\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p(f):=\frac{\partial(f\circ\varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr).$$ By the formula of Step 3 every $v\in T_pM$ has a unique expansion $$v=\sum_{i=1}^n v^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,\qquad v^i=v(x^i)=dx^i(v),$$ so these $n$ vectors form a basis and $\dim T_pM=n$. Under a change of chart $y=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}(x)$ the chain rule gives $$\frac{\partial}{\partial y^j}\Big|_p=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^j}\bigl(\psi(p)\bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,$$ so tangent coordinates transform by $v^i=\sum_j\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^j}w^j$ (contravariantly), with an invertible transition matrix.

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth. Define $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ by $dF_p[\gamma]:=[F\circ\gamma]$. It is well defined: if $\gamma_1\sim\gamma_2$, choose charts near $p$ and $F(p)$; the coordinate expression $\tilde F=\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}$ is smooth, so $$(\psi\circ F\circ\gamma_i)'(0)=D\tilde F\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)\bigl[(\varphi\circ\gamma_i)'(0)\bigr],$$ and equal velocities give equal image velocities. The map $dF_p$ is linear (in coordinates it is multiplication by a fixed matrix), and $$d(G\circ F)_p=dG_{F(p)}\circ dF_p,\qquad d(\mathrm{id}_M)_p=\mathrm{id}.$$ In derivation form $(dF_p v)(g)=v(g\circ F)$ for $g\in C^\infty(N)$. Thus the differential pushes tangent directions from $M$ to $N$, and composition corresponds to multiplication of matrices.

In bases the matrix is transparent: if $y^j=F^j(x)$, then $$dF_p\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p\Bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\partial F^j}{\partial x^i}(p)\frac{\partial}{\partial y^j}\Big|_{F(p)},$$ so the matrix of $dF_p$ is the Jacobian $(\partial F^j/\partial x^i)$ and $\operatorname{rank}dF_p$ is chart-independent. If $\dim M=\dim N=n$ and $dF_p$ is invertible, the inverse function theorem makes $F$ a local diffeomorphism near $p$, with $(dF_p)^{-1}=d(F^{-1})_{F(p)}$. Example: $S^2=F^{-1}(1)$ for $F(x)=|x|^2$ has $dF_p=2p^{\mathsf T}\ne0$, so by the regular level set theorem $T_pS^2=\ker dF_p=\{v:v\cdot p=0\}=p^\perp$. Mind the direction: the differential only maps $T_pM$ to $T_{F(p)}N$; when $F$ is not injective a vector field generally cannot be pushed forward globally, whereas forms can always be pulled back.

zh: 向量场是光滑截面 $X:M\to TM$，即 $\pi\circ X=\mathrm{id}_M$，且在每张图里 $$X=\sum_{i=1}^n X^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i},\qquad X^i\in C^\infty(U).$$ 等价地，$X$ 作用在函数上：$X(f)=df(X)$，它是实线性且满足莱布尼茨法则 $X(fg)=fX(g)+gX(f)$ 的算子；反之这样的导子必为上述形式，因为由泰勒公式它在坐标中是二阶导为零的一阶算子。全体光滑向量场记 $\mathfrak{X}(M)$，它是 $C^\infty(M)$-模：$(fX)(g)=fX(g)$。结论：向量场就是对函数求方向导数的一阶微分算子，光滑性就是系数光滑。

给定 $X$，积分曲线是光滑 $\gamma:I\to M$ 满足 $$\gamma'(t)=X\bigl(\gamma(t)\bigr),$$ 在图中即一阶方程组 $\dot x^i=X^i(x(t))$。因 $X^i$ 光滑（从而局部 Lipschitz），Picard–Lindelöf 定理给出：对每点 $p$ 存在 $\varepsilon_p>0$ 与唯一的解 $\gamma_p:(-\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_p)\to M$，$\gamma_p(0)=p$；不同图上的局部解在重叠区一致，故可拼接成唯一的极大积分曲线，其定义区间 $I_p$ 是含 $0$ 的开区间。唯一性还给出：两条极大积分曲线若在某一时刻同处一点，则整条重合；否则像集不交。于是极大积分曲线把 $M$ 分成互不相交的轨道。

令 $\varphi_t(p):=\gamma_p(t)$，定义域 $D=\{(t,p):t\in I_p\}$。由 ODE 解对初值的光滑依赖性，$D$ 是开集且 $\varphi:D\to M$ 光滑。基本性质：$$\varphi_0=\mathrm{id}_M,\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t(p)=X\bigl(\varphi_t(p)\bigr).$$ 半群性质：固定 $p$ 与 $s$，曲线 $t\mapsto\varphi_{s+t}(p)$ 与 $t\mapsto\varphi_s(\varphi_t(p))$ 都解同一 ODE，且在 $t=0$ 都等于 $\varphi_s(p)$，由唯一性二者在公共定义域上相等：$\varphi_{s+t}=\varphi_s\circ\varphi_t$。取 $s=-t$ 得 $\varphi_t\circ\varphi_{-t}=\mathrm{id}$，故每个 $\varphi_t$ 是局部微分同胚，逆为 $\varphi_{-t}$。若 $D=\mathbb{R}\times M$，称 $X$ 完备，此时 $\{\varphi_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ 是单参数微分同胚群。

李括号定义为导子的交换子：$$[X,Y](f):=X\bigl(Y(f)\bigr)-Y\bigl(X(f)\bigr).$$ 它仍是导子：把 $XY(fg)$ 与 $YX(fg)$ 展开，含 $X(f)Y(g)$ 与 $Y(f)X(g)$ 的交叉项相消，剩下 $f[X,Y](g)+g[X,Y](f)$。在坐标中 $$\begin{aligned}&[X,Y]=\sum_{k=1}^n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n X^i\frac{\partial Y^k}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}\\&\quad-\sum_{k=1}^n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n Y^i\frac{\partial X^k}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}.\end{aligned}$$ 推导：两边都是导子，只需比较作用在坐标函数 $x^k$ 上的值，链式法则即得上式。由定义立即有反称性 $[X,Y]=-[Y,X]$ 与雅可比恒等式 $$[[X,Y],Z]+[[Y,Z],X]+[[Z,X],Y]=0,$$ 后者展开后每项出现两次、符号相反。结论：$\mathfrak{X}(M)$ 是无穷维李代数。注意 $[fX,gY]=fg[X,Y]+f(Xg)Y-g(Yf)X$，故括号不是 $C^\infty(M)$-双线性的，它不是张量。

括号的几何意义是流的非交换性。设 $X,Y$ 的流分别为 $\varphi^X,\varphi^Y$，$p\in M$，$t$ 充分小使所有复合有定义。在图中把每个流按 $t$ 展开：$$\varphi^X_t(x)=x+tX(x)+\frac{t^2}{2}DX(x)\bigl[X(x)\bigr]+O(t^3),$$ 对 $Y$ 同理。把 $$\varphi^Y_{-t}\circ\varphi^X_{-t}\circ\varphi^Y_t\circ\varphi^X_t(p)$$ 逐次代入并按 $t$ 的幂整理：$O(t)$ 项抵消，$O(t^2)$ 中的 $\frac12DXX+\frac12DYY$ 也成对抵消，只剩 $$p+t^2\bigl(DY\cdot X-DX\cdot Y\bigr)(p)+O(t^3)=p+t^2[X,Y]_p+O(t^3).$$ 因此 $[X,Y]$ 是「先沿 $X$、再沿 $Y$ 各走 $t$，再依次退回」所得位移的二阶主部。特别地，$[X,Y]=0$ 时 $(\varphi^X_t)_*Y=Y$（因 $\frac{d}{dt}(\varphi^X_t)_*Y=(\varphi^X_t)_*[X,Y]=0$），故 $\varphi^X_t\circ\varphi^Y_s\circ\varphi^X_{-t}$ 与 $\varphi^Y_s$ 是同一向量场的流且初值相同，两流局部交换；反之若两流交换，由上面的展开得 $[X,Y]=0$。条件：$X,Y$ 至少 $C^2$，且 $t$ 足够小。

完备性。若 $M$ 紧且 $X$ 光滑，则存在 $\varepsilon>0$，使对任意 $p$ 积分曲线都在 $|t|<\varepsilon$ 上有定义：每点有邻域 $U_p$ 与时间 $\delta_p$，取有限子覆盖并用 Lebesgue 数即可让「起点在同一邻域内」的解有统一存在时间。于是对任意 $T$，用 $\lceil|T|/\varepsilon\rceil$ 步拼接即可定义 $\varphi_T$，唯一性保证拼接一致，故 $D=\mathbb{R}\times M$：紧流形上向量场必完备。非紧时可能失败：$X=x^2\partial_x$ 在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上的积分曲线为 $$x(t)=\frac{x_0}{1-x_0t}\quad(x_0>0),$$ 在 $t\to1/x_0$ 时爆破，无法延拓。奇点 $X(p)=0$ 处常值曲线是积分曲线，由唯一性 $\varphi_t(p)=p$ 对一切 $t$ 成立；反之若 $\varphi_t(p)=p$ 对一切 $t$ 成立，对 $t$ 在 $0$ 处求导得 $X(p)=0$。
en: A vector field is a smooth section $X:M\to TM$, i.e. $\pi\circ X=\mathrm{id}_M$, and in every chart $$X=\sum_{i=1}^n X^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i},\qquad X^i\in C^\infty(U).$$ Equivalently $X$ acts on functions by $X(f)=df(X)$: a real-linear operator satisfying the Leibniz rule $X(fg)=fX(g)+gX(f)$. Conversely every such derivation has the displayed form, because Taylor's formula shows that in coordinates it is a first-order operator with no second derivatives. The smooth vector fields form $\mathfrak{X}(M)$, a $C^\infty(M)$-module under $(fX)(g)=fX(g)$. Thus a vector field is a first-order differential operator, and smoothness means smooth coefficients.

Given $X$, an integral curve is a smooth $\gamma:I\to M$ with $$\gamma'(t)=X\bigl(\gamma(t)\bigr),$$ which in a chart is the first-order system $\dot x^i=X^i(x(t))$. Since the $X^i$ are smooth (hence locally Lipschitz), Picard–Lindelöf gives, for each $p$, some $\varepsilon_p>0$ and a unique solution $\gamma_p:(-\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_p)\to M$ with $\gamma_p(0)=p$; local solutions in different charts agree on overlaps, so they glue into a unique maximal integral curve with open interval $I_p\ni0$. Uniqueness also shows that two maximal integral curves which meet at one time coincide entirely, and otherwise have disjoint images. The maximal curves therefore foliate $M$ into disjoint orbits.

Set $\varphi_t(p):=\gamma_p(t)$ on the domain $D=\{(t,p):t\in I_p\}$. Smooth dependence of ODE solutions on initial data makes $D$ open and $\varphi:D\to M$ smooth. The basic properties are $$\varphi_0=\mathrm{id}_M,\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t(p)=X\bigl(\varphi_t(p)\bigr).$$ Semigroup law: fix $p$ and $s$; both $t\mapsto\varphi_{s+t}(p)$ and $t\mapsto\varphi_s(\varphi_t(p))$ solve the same ODE and agree at $t=0$, namely at $\varphi_s(p)$, so uniqueness gives $\varphi_{s+t}=\varphi_s\circ\varphi_t$ on the common domain. Taking $s=-t$ yields $\varphi_t\circ\varphi_{-t}=\mathrm{id}$, so each $\varphi_t$ is a local diffeomorphism with inverse $\varphi_{-t}$. If $D=\mathbb{R}\times M$, then $X$ is complete and $\{\varphi_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ is a one-parameter group of diffeomorphisms.

The Lie bracket is the commutator of derivations: $$[X,Y](f):=X\bigl(Y(f)\bigr)-Y\bigl(X(f)\bigr).$$ It is again a derivation: expanding $XY(fg)$ and $YX(fg)$, the mixed terms containing $X(f)Y(g)$ and $Y(f)X(g)$ cancel, leaving $f[X,Y](g)+g[X,Y](f)$. In coordinates $$\begin{aligned}&[X,Y]=\sum_{k=1}^n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n X^i\frac{\partial Y^k}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}\\&\quad-\sum_{k=1}^n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n Y^i\frac{\partial X^k}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}.\end{aligned}$$ Indeed both sides are derivations, so it suffices to compare them on the coordinate functions $x^k$, where the chain rule gives the displayed formula. The definition immediately yields antisymmetry $[X,Y]=-[Y,X]$ and the Jacobi identity $$[[X,Y],Z]+[[Y,Z],X]+[[Z,X],Y]=0,$$ since expansion produces each term twice with opposite signs. Hence $\mathfrak{X}(M)$ is an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra. Note $[fX,gY]=fg[X,Y]+f(Xg)Y-g(Yf)X$, so the bracket is not $C^\infty(M)$-bilinear and is not a tensor.

Geometrically the bracket measures non-commutativity of flows. Let $\varphi^X,\varphi^Y$ be the flows of $X,Y$ and fix $p\in M$, with $t$ small enough that all composites are defined. In a chart expand each flow in $t$: $$\varphi^X_t(x)=x+tX(x)+\frac{t^2}{2}DX(x)\bigl[X(x)\bigr]+O(t^3),$$ and likewise for $Y$. Substituting successively into $$\varphi^Y_{-t}\circ\varphi^X_{-t}\circ\varphi^Y_t\circ\varphi^X_t(p)$$ and collecting powers of $t$: the $O(t)$ terms cancel, the $\frac12DXX+\frac12DYY$ terms in $O(t^2)$ cancel in pairs, and only $$p+t^2\bigl(DY\cdot X-DX\cdot Y\bigr)(p)+O(t^3)=p+t^2[X,Y]_p+O(t^3)$$ remains. Thus $[X,Y]$ is the second-order principal part of the displacement obtained by going $t$ along $X$, then $t$ along $Y$, then back along both. In particular, if $[X,Y]=0$ then $(\varphi^X_t)_*Y=Y$ (because $\frac{d}{dt}(\varphi^X_t)_*Y=(\varphi^X_t)_*[X,Y]=0$), so $\varphi^X_t\circ\varphi^Y_s\circ\varphi^X_{-t}$ and $\varphi^Y_s$ are flows of the same field with the same initial value and hence coincide, giving local commutation; conversely, commuting flows force $[X,Y]=0$ by the expansion. Hypotheses: $X,Y$ at least $C^2$ and $t$ sufficiently small.

Completeness. If $M$ is compact and $X$ smooth, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that every integral curve is defined for $|t|<\varepsilon$ from any starting point: each point has a neighbourhood $U_p$ and a time $\delta_p$, and a finite subcover together with a Lebesgue number gives a uniform existence time for all starting points in one chart neighbourhood. Then for any $T$, composing $\lceil|T|/\varepsilon\rceil$ flow steps defines $\varphi_T$, and uniqueness makes the composition consistent, so $D=\mathbb{R}\times M$: every vector field on a compact manifold is complete. On non-compact manifolds this can fail: for $X=x^2\partial_x$ on $\mathbb{R}$ the integral curve is $$x(t)=\frac{x_0}{1-x_0t}\quad(x_0>0),$$ which blows up as $t\to1/x_0$ and cannot be extended. At a singularity $X(p)=0$ the constant curve is an integral curve, so $\varphi_t(p)=p$ for all $t$; conversely, if $\varphi_t(p)=p$ for all $t$, differentiating at $t=0$ gives $X(p)=0$.

zh: 固定 $p$，令 $V=T_pM$，$\dim V=n$。称 $\omega_p:V^k\to\mathbb{R}$ 为反对称 $k$ 重线性函数，若它对每个变量线性，且交换任意两个变量时变号：$$\omega_p(\dots,v_i,\dots,v_j,\dots)=-\omega_p(\dots,v_j,\dots,v_i,\dots).$$ 等价地，对任意置换 $\sigma\in S_k$ 有 $\omega_p(v_{\sigma(1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k)})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_k)$；特别地，两个变量相等时取值为零。这些函数构成向量空间 $\Lambda^k(T_pM)^*$。$k=0$ 时它就是 $\mathbb{R}$，$k=1$ 时它就是 $T_p^*M$。在整个流形上光滑地指定 $\omega_p$ 即得 $k$-形式，记 $\Omega^k(M)$；光滑指任意图中系数光滑。

取图 $(U,\varphi)$，记 $dx^i$ 为坐标函数 $x^i$ 的微分，$dx^I=dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$（$I=(i_1<\cdots<i_k)$）。每个 $k$-形式在 $U$ 上唯一写成 $$\begin{aligned}\omega&=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n}a_{i_1\cdots i_k}\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k},\\ a_I&=\omega\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i_1}},\dots,\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i_k}}\Bigr).\end{aligned}$$ 唯一性来自基的对偶性：$dx^I(\partial_{j_1},\dots,\partial_{j_k})=\det(\delta^{i_r}_{j_s})$，当 $J=I$ 时为 $1$，当 $J$ 是 $I$ 的置换时为符号，其余为 $0$。指标递增书写避免重复计数，独立分量共 $\binom{n}{k}$ 个；$k>n$ 时 $\binom{n}{k}=0$，只有零形式。$\omega$ 光滑当且仅当所有 $a_I$ 光滑。

外积把 $\alpha\in\Omega^k$ 与 $\beta\in\Omega^l$ 乘为 $k+l$ 形式。采用交替化约定 $$\begin{aligned}&(\alpha\wedge\beta)_p(v_1,\dots,v_{k+l})\\&\quad=\frac{1}{k!\,l!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_{k+l}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\\&\qquad\cdot\alpha_p(v_{\sigma(1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k)})\,\beta_p(v_{\sigma(k+1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k+l)}).\end{aligned}$$ 它双线性、结合，并满足分次交换律 $$\alpha\wedge\beta=(-1)^{kl}\beta\wedge\alpha.$$ 证明：把前 $k$ 个指标与后 $l$ 个指标整体交换的置换，其符号为 $(-1)^{kl}$，代入定义即把 $\alpha\wedge\beta$ 的求和变成 $\beta\wedge\alpha$ 的求和。推论：$dx^i\wedge dx^j=-dx^j\wedge dx^i$，$dx^i\wedge dx^i=0$；两个 1-形式反交换，而偶数次形式之间交换。注意 1-形式 $\alpha$ 满足 $\alpha\wedge\alpha=0$，但次数为偶的 $\omega$ 未必有 $\omega\wedge\omega=0$（例如 $\mathbb{R}^4$ 上 $\omega=dx^1\wedge dx^2+dx^3\wedge dx^4$ 满足 $\omega\wedge\omega=2\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4\ne0$）。

拉回。设 $F:M\to N$ 光滑，$\omega\in\Omega^k(N)$。定义 $$(F^*\omega)_p(v_1,\dots,v_k):=\omega_{F(p)}\bigl(dF_pv_1,\dots,dF_pv_k\bigr),\qquad v_i\in T_pM.$$ 右边只用到 $F$ 的切映射，故 $F$ 不必可逆；由 $dF_p$ 线性，$F^*\omega$ 仍反对称 $k$ 重线性，光滑性由 $F$ 光滑与链式法则得到。拉回保结构：$$F^*(\omega\wedge\eta)=F^*\omega\wedge F^*\eta,\qquad (G\circ F)^*=F^*\circ G^*.$$ 坐标公式：若 $F$ 由 $y^j=F^j(x)$ 给出，则 $F^*\omega=\sum_I a_I(F(x))\,dF^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dF^{i_k}$；当 $k=n=m$ 时 $$F^*(dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n)=\det\Bigl(\frac{\partial F^j}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n,$$ 雅可比行列式自动出现。

体积形式与定向。由行列式公式 $$dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\det\bigl(v_1,\dots,v_n\bigr)$$（右端是以 $v_j$ 为列的矩阵），该 $n$-形式在基上取 $\pm1$，在退化组上取 $0$。若 $n$-形式 $\Omega$ 处处非零，称它为体积形式；它给出定向：基 $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ 为正，当且仅当 $\Omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_n)>0$。在坐标中 $\Omega=h\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$，$h$ 处处非零；连通流形上两个体积形式相差一个处处非零函数，故恰有两个定向 $\Omega$ 与 $-\Omega$。于是：连通 $n$ 维流形可定向，当且仅当存在处处非零的 $n$-形式；莫比乌斯带不存在这样的形式，故不可定向。

例：$F(r,\theta)=(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)$，$r>0$。先算 1-形式拉回：$$F^*dx=\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta,\qquad F^*dy=\sin\theta\,dr+r\cos\theta\,d\theta.$$ 再用 $F^*(\alpha\wedge\beta)=F^*\alpha\wedge F^*\beta$ 与 $dr\wedge dr=d\theta\wedge d\theta=0$：$$\begin{aligned}F^*(dx\wedge dy)&=(\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta)\wedge(\sin\theta\,dr+r\cos\theta\,d\theta)\\&=r\cos^2\theta\,dr\wedge d\theta-r\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\wedge dr\\&=r(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)\,dr\wedge d\theta=r\,dr\wedge d\theta.\end{aligned}$$ 这正是面积元 $dx\,dy=r\,dr\,d\theta$，雅可比 $r>0$ 说明该参数化保定向。对比：形式总能拉回（方向与 $F$ 相反），而向量场只有在 $F$ 为微分同胚时才能自然推前；1-形式与向量场的配对由 $\omega(X)=\iota_X\omega$ 给出。
en: Fix $p$ and put $V=T_pM$, $\dim V=n$. A map $\omega_p:V^k\to\mathbb{R}$ is alternating $k$-linear if it is linear in each variable and changes sign when two variables are interchanged: $$\omega_p(\dots,v_i,\dots,v_j,\dots)=-\omega_p(\dots,v_j,\dots,v_i,\dots).$$ Equivalently $\omega_p(v_{\sigma(1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k)})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_k)$ for every permutation $\sigma\in S_k$; in particular the value is zero when two arguments coincide. These maps form a vector space $\Lambda^k(T_pM)^*$. For $k=0$ it is $\mathbb{R}$, and for $k=1$ it is $T_p^*M$. Assigning $\omega_p$ smoothly over $M$ gives a $k$-form, written $\omega\in\Omega^k(M)$; smooth means smooth coefficients in every chart.

In a chart $(U,\varphi)$ let $dx^i$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^i$ and $dx^I=dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$ for $I=(i_1<\cdots<i_k)$. Every $k$-form on $U$ is uniquely $$\begin{aligned}\omega&=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n}a_{i_1\cdots i_k}\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k},\\ a_I&=\omega\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i_1}},\dots,\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i_k}}\Bigr).\end{aligned}$$ Uniqueness comes from duality of the basis: $dx^I(\partial_{j_1},\dots,\partial_{j_k})=\det(\delta^{i_r}_{j_s})$, which is $1$ when $J=I$, the sign of the permutation when $J$ is a permutation of $I$, and $0$ otherwise. Writing indices increasingly avoids double counting, leaving $\binom{n}{k}$ independent components; for $k>n$, $\binom{n}{k}=0$ and only the zero form exists. The form $\omega$ is smooth exactly when all $a_I$ are smooth.

The wedge product multiplies $\alpha\in\Omega^k$ and $\beta\in\Omega^l$ into a $(k+l)$-form. With the alternation convention $$\begin{aligned}&(\alpha\wedge\beta)_p(v_1,\dots,v_{k+l})\\&\quad=\frac{1}{k!\,l!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_{k+l}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\\&\qquad\cdot\alpha_p(v_{\sigma(1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k)})\,\beta_p(v_{\sigma(k+1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k+l)}),\end{aligned}$$ it is bilinear, associative, and satisfies graded commutativity $$\alpha\wedge\beta=(-1)^{kl}\beta\wedge\alpha.$$ Proof: the permutation exchanging the first $k$ and last $l$ indices as blocks has sign $(-1)^{kl}$, and substituting it into the definition turns the sum for $\alpha\wedge\beta$ into the sum for $\beta\wedge\alpha$. Consequences: $dx^i\wedge dx^j=-dx^j\wedge dx^i$ and $dx^i\wedge dx^i=0$; two 1-forms anticommute, while even-degree forms commute. Note that a 1-form $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha\wedge\alpha=0$, but an even-degree $\omega$ need not satisfy $\omega\wedge\omega=0$ (e.g. $\omega=dx^1\wedge dx^2+dx^3\wedge dx^4$ on $\mathbb{R}^4$ has $\omega\wedge\omega=2\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4\ne0$).

Pullback. Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth and $\omega\in\Omega^k(N)$. Define $$(F^*\omega)_p(v_1,\dots,v_k):=\omega_{F(p)}\bigl(dF_pv_1,\dots,dF_pv_k\bigr),\qquad v_i\in T_pM.$$ The right side uses only the differential of $F$, so $F$ need not be invertible; linearity of $dF_p$ makes $F^*\omega$ alternating $k$-linear, and smoothness follows from smoothness of $F$ and the chain rule. Pullback preserves structure: $$F^*(\omega\wedge\eta)=F^*\omega\wedge F^*\eta,\qquad (G\circ F)^*=F^*\circ G^*.$$ In coordinates, if $F$ is given by $y^j=F^j(x)$, then $F^*\omega=\sum_I a_I(F(x))\,dF^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dF^{i_k}$; when $k=n=m$, $$F^*(dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n)=\det\Bigl(\frac{\partial F^j}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n,$$ so the Jacobian determinant appears automatically.

Volume forms and orientation. The determinant formula $$dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\det\bigl(v_1,\dots,v_n\bigr)$$ (the matrix has the $v_j$ as columns) shows that this $n$-form takes the values $\pm1$ on bases and $0$ on degenerate tuples. A nowhere-vanishing $n$-form $\Omega$ is a volume form; it defines an orientation by declaring a basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ positive iff $\Omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_n)>0$. In coordinates $\Omega=h\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ with $h$ nowhere zero; on a connected manifold two volume forms differ by a nowhere-zero function, so there are exactly two orientations $\Omega$ and $-\Omega$. Hence a connected $n$-manifold is orientable if and only if it carries a nowhere-vanishing $n$-form; the Möbius band carries none and is non-orientable.

Example: $F(r,\theta)=(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)$ with $r>0$. First pull back the 1-forms: $$F^*dx=\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta,\qquad F^*dy=\sin\theta\,dr+r\cos\theta\,d\theta.$$ Then use $F^*(\alpha\wedge\beta)=F^*\alpha\wedge F^*\beta$ and $dr\wedge dr=d\theta\wedge d\theta=0$: $$\begin{aligned}F^*(dx\wedge dy)&=(\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta)\wedge(\sin\theta\,dr+r\cos\theta\,d\theta)\\&=r\cos^2\theta\,dr\wedge d\theta-r\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\wedge dr\\&=r(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)\,dr\wedge d\theta=r\,dr\wedge d\theta.\end{aligned}$$ This is the area element $dx\,dy=r\,dr\,d\theta$, and the Jacobian $r>0$ shows the parametrization is orientation-preserving. Comparison: forms can always be pulled back (against the direction of $F$), whereas vector fields push forward naturally only under diffeomorphisms; a 1-form pairs with a vector field through $\omega(X)=\iota_X\omega$.

zh: 外微分是满足以下四条的唯一族算子 $d:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{k+1}(M)$：（i）$\mathbb{R}$-线性；（ii）分次莱布尼茨律 $$d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d\omega\wedge\eta+(-1)^{k}\omega\wedge d\eta,\qquad k=|\omega|;$$（iii）$d^2=0$；（iv）对 $f\in C^\infty(M)$ 与 $v\in T_pM$，$df_p(v)=v(f)$。唯一性：在图中写 $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$，由（ii）与 $d(dx^I)=0$（每个 $dx^I$ 是 1-形式的楔积，而 $d^2x^i=0$）得 $$d\omega=\sum_I da_I\wedge dx^I,$$ 右边被（i）（iv）完全确定；不同图给出的表达式由转换函数的链式法则一致，故 $d$ 存在且唯一。注意 $d(f\omega)=df\wedge\omega+f\,d\omega$，故 $d$ 不是 $C^\infty(M)$-线性的。

局部公式与低次例子。对 $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$，$$d\omega=\sum_I\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{\partial a_I}{\partial x^j}\,dx^j\wedge dx^I=\sum_I da_I\wedge dx^I.$$ 0-形式：$df=\sum_i\partial_i f\,dx^i$。1-形式（$n=2$）：设 $\omega=P\,dx+Q\,dy$，则 $$\begin{aligned}d\omega&=dP\wedge dx+dQ\wedge dy\\&=(P_x\,dx+P_y\,dy)\wedge dx+(Q_x\,dx+Q_y\,dy)\wedge dy\\&=(Q_x-P_y)\,dx\wedge dy,\end{aligned}$$ 其中用了 $dx\wedge dx=dy\wedge dy=0$ 与 $dy\wedge dx=-dx\wedge dy$。系数 $Q_x-P_y$ 正是格林公式中的被积函数，也是旋度的 $z$ 分量。结论：$d$ 在坐标中就是「系数求普通微分再外积」。

$d^2=0$。设 $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$，$a_I\in C^2$。连续作用两次：$$d^2\omega=\sum_I\sum_{j,i}\frac{\partial^2 a_I}{\partial x^i\partial x^j}\,dx^i\wedge dx^j\wedge dx^I.$$ 把 $(i,j)$ 与 $(j,i)$ 两项配对：由 Schwarz 定理 $\partial_i\partial_j a_I=\partial_j\partial_i a_I$（系数相同），而 $dx^i\wedge dx^j=-dx^j\wedge dx^i$（符号相反），故两项之和为零；$i=j$ 时 $dx^i\wedge dx^i=0$。于是 $d^2\omega=0$。条件 $a_I\in C^2$ 不可省：证明用到了混合偏导可交换。结论：$d^2=0$ 在坐标中就是「二阶偏导对称、外积反对称」这两件事的相容性，它使 $\{\Omega^k(M),d\}$ 成为上链复形。

分次莱布尼茨律的符号。只需对单项式 $\omega=f\,dx^I$、$\eta=g\,dx^J$ 验证，$k=|I|$、$l=|J|$，再用双线性推广。由 $d(dx^I)=0$ 与普通乘积法则：$$d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d(fg\,dx^I\wedge dx^J)=(g\,df+f\,dg)\wedge dx^I\wedge dx^J.$$ 第一项就是 $d\omega\wedge\eta$；第二项中 $dg$ 是 1-形式，把它从 $dx^I$ 的右边移到左边要跨过 $k$ 个 1-形式，每次换序变号，故 $$f\,dg\wedge dx^I\wedge dx^J=(-1)^k f\,dx^I\wedge dg\wedge dx^J=(-1)^k\omega\wedge d\eta.$$ 相加即得 $d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d\omega\wedge\eta+(-1)^k\omega\wedge d\eta$。结论：符号只由左因子次数 $k$ 决定，不能写成 $(-1)^l$ 或省略；$k$ 为偶数时两项同号相加，为奇数时第二项反号。

闭形式与恰当形式。称 $\omega$ 闭若 $d\omega=0$，恰当若 $\omega=d\eta$。由 $d^2=0$，恰当必闭：$d\omega=d^2\eta=0$。反向一般不成立。例：在 $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ 上 $$\omega=\frac{-y\,dx+x\,dy}{x^2+y^2}=P\,dx+Q\,dy,$$ 直接求导得 $$Q_x=\frac{(x^2+y^2)-2x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}=\frac{y^2-x^2}{r^4}=P_y,$$ 故 $d\omega=(Q_x-P_y)\,dx\wedge dy=0$，$\omega$ 闭。但若 $\omega=d\eta$，沿单位圆 $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t)$ 有 $\oint_\gamma\omega=\int_0^{2\pi}dt=2\pi$，而恰当形式沿闭曲线积分必为 $\eta(\gamma(2\pi))-\eta(\gamma(0))=0$，矛盾，故 $\omega$ 不恰当。

庞加莱引理与其条件。设 $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ 关于某点星形（特别地 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 本身或凸域），$\omega\in\Omega^k(U)$ 闭，$k\ge1$。定义同伦算子 $$(K\omega)_x(v_1,\dots,v_{k-1})=\int_0^1 t^{k-1}\,\omega_{tx}\bigl(x,v_1,\dots,v_{k-1}\bigr)\,dt,$$ 直接计算可得链同伦公式 $$d(K\omega)+K(d\omega)=\omega,\qquad k\ge1.$$ 于是 $d\omega=0$ 时 $\omega=d(K\omega)$：每个闭形式都恰当。条件「星形/可缩」不可省：$\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ 不星形，第 5 步的 $\omega$ 闭而不恰当；$H^1_{dR}(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\})\cong\mathbb{R}$ 正度量了这个「洞」。最后，$d$ 与拉回交换：$F^*(d\omega)=d(F^*\omega)$（坐标中两边都等于对 $a_I\circ F$ 求偏导再外积），故 $d$ 是光滑流形范畴内的自然算子；在 $\mathbb{R}^3$ 中配合度规与 Hodge 星号，$d$ 沿 $0\to1\to2\to3$ 形式链分别对应梯度、旋度、散度，$d^2=0$ 对应 $\operatorname{curl}\nabla=0$ 与 $\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}=0$。
en: The exterior derivative is the unique family of operators $d:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{k+1}(M)$ satisfying: (i) $\mathbb{R}$-linearity; (ii) the graded Leibniz rule $$d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d\omega\wedge\eta+(-1)^{k}\omega\wedge d\eta,\qquad k=|\omega|;$$ (iii) $d^2=0$; (iv) $df_p(v)=v(f)$ for $f\in C^\infty(M)$ and $v\in T_pM$. Uniqueness: write $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$ in a chart. By (ii) and $d(dx^I)=0$ (each $dx^I$ is a wedge of 1-forms and $d^2x^i=0$), $$d\omega=\sum_I da_I\wedge dx^I,$$ whose right side is completely determined by (i) and (iv); expressions from different charts agree by the chain rule for transition maps, so $d$ exists and is unique. Note $d(f\omega)=df\wedge\omega+f\,d\omega$, so $d$ is not $C^\infty(M)$-linear.

Local formula and low-degree examples. For $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$, $$d\omega=\sum_I\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{\partial a_I}{\partial x^j}\,dx^j\wedge dx^I=\sum_I da_I\wedge dx^I.$$ For a 0-form, $df=\sum_i\partial_i f\,dx^i$. For a 1-form in $n=2$, write $\omega=P\,dx+Q\,dy$; then $$\begin{aligned}d\omega&=dP\wedge dx+dQ\wedge dy\\&=(P_x\,dx+P_y\,dy)\wedge dx+(Q_x\,dx+Q_y\,dy)\wedge dy\\&=(Q_x-P_y)\,dx\wedge dy,\end{aligned}$$ using $dx\wedge dx=dy\wedge dy=0$ and $dy\wedge dx=-dx\wedge dy$. The coefficient $Q_x-P_y$ is exactly the integrand in Green's theorem and the $z$-component of the curl. Thus in coordinates $d$ differentiates the coefficients and wedges.

$d^2=0$. Let $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$ with $a_I\in C^2$. Applying $d$ twice, $$d^2\omega=\sum_I\sum_{j,i}\frac{\partial^2 a_I}{\partial x^i\partial x^j}\,dx^i\wedge dx^j\wedge dx^I.$$ Pair the terms $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$: Schwarz's theorem gives equal coefficients $\partial_i\partial_j a_I=\partial_j\partial_i a_I$, while $dx^i\wedge dx^j=-dx^j\wedge dx^i$ gives opposite signs, so each pair cancels; for $i=j$, $dx^i\wedge dx^i=0$. Hence $d^2\omega=0$. The hypothesis $a_I\in C^2$ cannot be dropped, since the proof uses equality of mixed partials. Thus $d^2=0$ is precisely the compatibility of symmetric second partials with the antisymmetric wedge, and it makes $\{\Omega^k(M),d\}$ a cochain complex.

The sign in the graded Leibniz rule. It suffices to check monomials $\omega=f\,dx^I$, $\eta=g\,dx^J$ with $k=|I|$, $l=|J|$, then extend by bilinearity. Using $d(dx^I)=0$ and the ordinary product rule, $$d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d(fg\,dx^I\wedge dx^J)=(g\,df+f\,dg)\wedge dx^I\wedge dx^J.$$ The first term is $d\omega\wedge\eta$. In the second, $dg$ is a 1-form; moving it from the right of $dx^I$ to the left crosses $k$ one-forms, each crossing changing the sign, so $$f\,dg\wedge dx^I\wedge dx^J=(-1)^k f\,dx^I\wedge dg\wedge dx^J=(-1)^k\omega\wedge d\eta.$$ Adding gives $d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d\omega\wedge\eta+(-1)^k\omega\wedge d\eta$. Hence the sign is fixed by the degree $k$ of the left factor and may not be replaced by $(-1)^l$ or omitted; for even $k$ the two terms add with the same sign, for odd $k$ the second is reversed.

Closed and exact forms. A form is closed if $d\omega=0$ and exact if $\omega=d\eta$. Since $d^2=0$, exact implies closed: $d\omega=d^2\eta=0$. The converse fails in general. Example: on $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$, $$\omega=\frac{-y\,dx+x\,dy}{x^2+y^2}=P\,dx+Q\,dy,$$ and direct differentiation gives $$Q_x=\frac{(x^2+y^2)-2x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}=\frac{y^2-x^2}{r^4}=P_y,$$ so $d\omega=(Q_x-P_y)\,dx\wedge dy=0$ and $\omega$ is closed. But if $\omega=d\eta$, then along the unit circle $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t)$ one has $\oint_\gamma\omega=\int_0^{2\pi}dt=2\pi$, whereas an exact form integrates to $\eta(\gamma(2\pi))-\eta(\gamma(0))=0$ over a closed curve—a contradiction, so $\omega$ is not exact.

The Poincaré lemma and its hypothesis. Let $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be star-shaped with respect to some point (in particular $\mathbb{R}^n$ itself or a convex domain), and let $\omega\in\Omega^k(U)$ be closed with $k\ge1$. Define the homotopy operator $$(K\omega)_x(v_1,\dots,v_{k-1})=\int_0^1 t^{k-1}\,\omega_{tx}\bigl(x,v_1,\dots,v_{k-1}\bigr)\,dt.$$ A direct computation gives the chain-homotopy identity $$d(K\omega)+K(d\omega)=\omega,\qquad k\ge1.$$ Hence if $d\omega=0$, then $\omega=d(K\omega)$: every closed form is exact. The star-shaped (or contractible) hypothesis is essential: $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ is not star-shaped, and the form of Step 5 is closed but not exact; $H^1_{dR}(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\})\cong\mathbb{R}$ measures exactly this hole. Finally, $d$ commutes with pullback: $F^*(d\omega)=d(F^*\omega)$ (in coordinates both sides differentiate $a_I\circ F$ and wedge), so $d$ is a natural operator of smooth manifolds; on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a metric and the Hodge star, $d$ encodes gradient, curl and divergence along the chain of $0$-, $1$-, $2$-, $3$-forms, and $d^2=0$ becomes $\operatorname{curl}\nabla=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}=0$.

zh: 定向。设 $M$ 是 $n$ 维光滑流形。一个定向可由图册给出：要求所有转换函数满足 $$\det D\bigl(\varphi_\beta\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1}\bigr)(x)>0$$ 在重叠区恒成立。等价地，定向由处处非零的 $n$-形式（体积形式）$\Omega$ 给出：把满足 $\Omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_n)>0$ 的基定为正基。两者等价：给定 $\Omega$，在图中写 $\Omega=h\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$，$h\ne0$，只取 $h>0$ 的图，则转换函数的雅可比等于 $h_\alpha/h_\beta>0$；反之给定正雅可比图册，用单位分解把各图的 $dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ 乘以非负系数拼成整体 $\Omega$。连通可定向流形恰有两个定向。莫比乌斯带两者都不满足，故不可定向。

局部积分。设 $\omega\in\Omega^n(M)$ 的支撑含于一张定向坐标卡 $(U,\varphi)$，在图中 $$\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n\qquad\bigl(f\in C_c(\varphi(U))\bigr),$$ 其中 $f$ 连续且紧支撑（更一般地，只要求 $f$ 可积）。定义 $$\int_M\omega:=\int_{\varphi(U)}f(x^1,\dots,x^n)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n,$$ 右端是普通的 $n$ 重（黎曼或勒贝格）积分。这是定义，不是定理；它把形式的积分化为系数函数的积分。条件：$f$ 可积（连续且紧支撑时自动可积），$\omega$ 是顶次形式——低于 $n$ 次的形式在 $n$ 维流形上没有这种积分。

与坐标卡无关。设另一张定向卡 $(V,\psi)$，$y=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}(x)$，在重叠区 $$\begin{aligned}\omega&=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n\\&=f\det\Bigl(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\Bigr)dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n\\&=:\tilde f\,dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n.\end{aligned}$$ 普通换元公式给出 $$\begin{aligned}&\int f(x)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n\\&\quad=\int f\bigl(x(y)\bigr)\Bigl|\det\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\Bigr|\,dy^1\cdots dy^n.\end{aligned}$$ 两张卡定向相容，故 $\det(\partial x/\partial y)=\det D(\varphi\circ\psi^{-1})>0$，绝对值可以去掉，右端恰是 $\int\tilde f\,dy$。结论：局部积分在重叠区一致；定向的唯一作用就是让雅可比的正负号与形式自带的符号相匹配，从而不需要绝对值。

整体积分。取局部有限定向图册 $\{(U_i,\varphi_i)\}$ 与从属的单位分解 $\{\rho_i\}$：$\rho_i\in C_c^\infty(U_i)$，$0\le\rho_i\le1$，$\sum_i\rho_i=1$（每点附近只有有限项非零）。对紧支撑的 $\omega\in\Omega^n(M)$，定义 $$\int_M\omega:=\sum_i\int_{U_i}\rho_i\,\omega.$$ 每一项的支撑紧含于 $U_i$，由第 2 步有定义；局部有限性使和式中每点只有有限项非零，故求和有意义。与选择无关：若 $\{\sigma_j\}$ 是另一组单位分解，则 $$\sum_i\int\rho_i\omega=\sum_i\sum_j\int\rho_i\sigma_j\omega=\sum_j\int\sigma_j\omega,$$ 中间交换求和由局部有限性保证，且 $\sum_i\rho_i=\sum_j\sigma_j=1$。结论：$\int_M$ 是 $\Omega^n_c(M)$ 上的线性泛函；若 $M$ 不紧，则需 $\omega$ 紧支撑（或绝对可积）才能保证收敛。

边界定向与 Stokes。设 $M$ 紧、可定向、带光滑边界，$\dim M=n$。在 $p\in\partial M$ 处有直和 $T_pM=T_p\partial M\oplus\mathbb{R}
u$，$
u$ 为外法向。约定：$\partial M$ 的基 $(e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})$ 为正，当且仅当 $(
u,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})$ 是 $T_pM$ 的正基（「外法向优先」）。模型情形 $\mathbb{H}^n=\{x_n\ge0\}$、标准定向 $dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$：外法向 $
u=-\partial_n$，而 $$\det(-\partial_n,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})=(-1)^n\det(e_1,\dots,e_{n-1},e_n),$$ 故 $\partial\mathbb{H}^n=\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ 的诱导定向是标准定向乘以 $(-1)^n$。在此约定下 Stokes 公式为 $$\int_M d\omega=\int_{\partial M}\omega,\qquad \omega\in\Omega^{n-1}(M),$$ 且 $M$ 紧、$\partial M$ 光滑、$\omega$ 为 $C^1$（$M$ 不紧时要求 $\omega$ 紧支撑）。符号检验：取 $\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{n-1}$，则 $d\omega=(-1)^{n-1}\partial_nf\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$，故 $\int_Md\omega=(-1)^{n-1}\int_{\mathbb{H}^n}\partial_nf=(-1)^n\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n-1}}f(x,0)\,dx$，与上面诱导定向给出的 $\int_{\partial M}\omega$ 一致。

例与不可定向情形。单位圆盘 $D=\{x^2+y^2\le1\}$ 取标准定向 $dx\wedge dy$，$\omega=x\,dy$，$d\omega=dx\wedge dy$。则 $$\int_Dd\omega=\operatorname{area}(D)=\pi,\qquad \int_{\partial D}\omega=\int_0^{2\pi}\cos^2t\,dt=\pi,$$ 边界取逆时针（外法向优先在 $D$ 上确为逆时针），Stokes 成立。再如 $S^2$ 取外法向，$\omega=x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy$，$d\omega=3\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$，故 $\int_{S^2}\omega=\int_{B^3}3\,dV=4\pi$，等于 $S^2$ 的面积；把参数化次序颠倒则得 $-4\pi$。若 $M$ 不可定向（莫比乌斯带），顶次形式无法整体积分，但仍可积分密度 $|\omega|$（如面积元 $\sqrt{EG-F^2}\,du\,dv$）；Stokes 在链上使用时不要求 $M$ 整体可定向。
en: Orientation. Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold. An orientation can be given by an atlas whose transition maps satisfy $$\det D\bigl(\varphi_\beta\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1}\bigr)(x)>0$$ on every overlap. Equivalently, an orientation is given by a nowhere-vanishing $n$-form (volume form) $\Omega$: declare a basis positive when $\Omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_n)>0$. The two descriptions agree: given $\Omega$, write $\Omega=h\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ in a chart with $h\ne0$ and keep only charts with $h>0$; then the transition Jacobian equals $h_\alpha/h_\beta>0$. Conversely, given a positive-Jacobian atlas, a partition of unity combines the local $dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ with nonnegative coefficients into a global $\Omega$. A connected orientable manifold has exactly two orientations. The Möbius band admits neither, hence is non-orientable.

Local integral. Let $\omega\in\Omega^n(M)$ have support inside an oriented chart $(U,\varphi)$, where $$\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n\qquad\bigl(f\in C_c(\varphi(U))\bigr),$$ with $f$ continuous and compactly supported (more generally, $f$ integrable). Define $$\int_M\omega:=\int_{\varphi(U)}f(x^1,\dots,x^n)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n,$$ the ordinary $n$-fold (Riemann or Lebesgue) integral on the right. This is a definition, not a theorem; it reduces the integral of a form to the integral of its coefficient. Hypotheses: $f$ integrable (automatic for continuous compactly supported $f$), and $\omega$ of top degree—forms of degree below $n$ have no such integral on an $n$-manifold.

Chart independence. Let $(V,\psi)$ be another oriented chart and $y=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}(x)$. On the overlap, $$\begin{aligned}\omega&=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n\\&=f\det\Bigl(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\Bigr)dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n\\&=:\tilde f\,dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n.\end{aligned}$$ The substitution formula gives $$\begin{aligned}&\int f(x)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n\\&\quad=\int f\bigl(x(y)\bigr)\Bigl|\det\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\Bigr|\,dy^1\cdots dy^n.\end{aligned}$$ The charts are compatibly oriented, so $\det(\partial x/\partial y)=\det D(\varphi\circ\psi^{-1})>0$ and the absolute value can be dropped; the right side is exactly $\int\tilde f\,dy$. Hence the local integrals agree on overlaps; the sole role of the orientation is to match the sign of the Jacobian with the sign carried by the form, making the absolute value unnecessary.

Global integral. Choose a locally finite oriented atlas $\{(U_i,\varphi_i)\}$ and a subordinate partition of unity $\{\rho_i\}$: $\rho_i\in C_c^\infty(U_i)$, $0\le\rho_i\le1$, $\sum_i\rho_i=1$ (only finitely many terms are nonzero near each point). For compactly supported $\omega\in\Omega^n(M)$ define $$\int_M\omega:=\sum_i\int_{U_i}\rho_i\,\omega.$$ Each term has support compactly contained in $U_i$ and is defined by Step 2; local finiteness makes the sum finite near each point, so it is meaningful. It is independent of choices: for another partition $\{\sigma_j\}$, $$\sum_i\int\rho_i\omega=\sum_i\sum_j\int\rho_i\sigma_j\omega=\sum_j\int\sigma_j\omega,$$ where exchanging the sums is justified by local finiteness and $\sum_i\rho_i=\sum_j\sigma_j=1$. Hence $\int_M$ is a linear functional on $\Omega^n_c(M)$; if $M$ is not compact, $\omega$ must be compactly supported (or absolutely integrable) for convergence.

Boundary orientation and Stokes. Let $M$ be compact, orientable, with smooth boundary, $\dim M=n$. At $p\in\partial M$ there is a direct sum $T_pM=T_p\partial M\oplus\mathbb{R}
u$ with $
u$ the outward normal. Convention: a basis $(e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})$ of $T_p\partial M$ is positive iff $(
u,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})$ is a positive basis of $T_pM$ (“outward normal first”). In the model $\mathbb{H}^n=\{x_n\ge0\}$ with the standard orientation $dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$, the outward normal is $
u=-\partial_n$, and $$\det(-\partial_n,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})=(-1)^n\det(e_1,\dots,e_{n-1},e_n),$$ so the induced orientation on $\partial\mathbb{H}^n=\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ is $(-1)^n$ times the standard one. With this convention Stokes' theorem reads $$\int_M d\omega=\int_{\partial M}\omega,\qquad \omega\in\Omega^{n-1}(M),$$ for compact $M$, smooth $\partial M$ and $C^1$ $\omega$ (compactly supported when $M$ is not compact). Sign check: for $\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{n-1}$, $d\omega=(-1)^{n-1}\partial_nf\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$, hence $\int_Md\omega=(-1)^{n-1}\int_{\mathbb{H}^n}\partial_nf=(-1)^n\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n-1}}f(x,0)\,dx$, matching $\int_{\partial M}\omega$ computed with the induced orientation above.

Examples and the non-orientable case. On the unit disk $D=\{x^2+y^2\le1\}$ with the standard orientation $dx\wedge dy$, take $\omega=x\,dy$, so $d\omega=dx\wedge dy$. Then $$\int_Dd\omega=\operatorname{area}(D)=\pi,\qquad \int_{\partial D}\omega=\int_0^{2\pi}\cos^2t\,dt=\pi,$$ with the boundary oriented counterclockwise (which is what “outward normal first” gives on $D$), so Stokes holds. Likewise on $S^2$ with the outward orientation, $\omega=x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy$ has $d\omega=3\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, so $\int_{S^2}\omega=\int_{B^3}3\,dV=4\pi$, the area of $S^2$; reversing the parametrization gives $-4\pi$. If $M$ is non-orientable (the Möbius band), top forms cannot be integrated globally, but densities such as the area element $\sqrt{EG-F^2}\,du\,dv$ still can; Stokes on chains does not require $M$ to be globally orientable.
